cfo_summary: Total available cash is $151,245 against a true bank balance of $255,208. After $29,937 in external payments and no intercompany transfers, projected end of week is $121,308. Twenty one bills, all approved, all operating. No management fees and no distributions on this run.

October rent lifted available cash $85,447 in one week. Eight of nine entities improved. Countryside projects to $55,003, Winterwood to $26,376, Four Seasons to $23,460 and Decade Acres to $15,745. This is the strongest portfolio position of the year.

Uncleared transactions are $103,963, the highest on record. True bank is $255,208 against available of $151,245. Countryside carries $42,497 of it, Country Aire $15,992, Winterwood $11,392 and GRP $26,333. The gap is large enough that true bank and available tell materially different stories this week.

GRP is at negative $23,813 available on a true bank balance of $2,520. The October management fees of $30,041 landed last week and are already consumed. There are no fees on this run, so nothing here corrects it. GRP projects to negative $26,940, the worst position recorded. This is the seventh negative opening in fifteen weeks.

GRP needs roughly $27,000 and Countryside can cover it four times over. Countryside projects to $55,003, Winterwood to $26,376 and Four Seasons to $23,460. Unlike most weeks, funding GRP this week costs the portfolio nothing in flexibility.

Both Royal Supply invoices are on this run early. $3,367.73 and $894.68 were Net 30 from 9/25 and not due until around 10/23. With rent landed there is no reason to hold them, but they could be deferred two more weeks if the cash were needed elsewhere.
Bookkeeping By Beth is $2,014.60 for 71.95 hours, covering two weeks and marked final invoice, against a typical weekly run of roughly $1,200 to $1,400.
Group Group sits at $83 for the sixth consecutive week. Distributions to it usually run in week three, so an October distribution would be due around 10/16.

for_ownership.label: Projected end-of-week cash
for_ownership.paragraph: We close this week at roughly $121,300 across all accounts, the strongest position of the year. October rent landed and lifted cash by about $85,000, with eight of the nine accounts improving. The bill run of $29,900 is all routine operating work, no management fees and no distributions. The one exception to the good picture is Golden Rule Practices, which is negative about $26,900 after its bills. The October management fees it received last week have already been spent on closing costs and loan payments, and there are no fees this week to replenish it. Countryside is holding $55,000 and can cover the gap easily, which is not usually the case. One number worth knowing: about $104,000 of payments are written but have not yet cleared the bank, the largest backlog we have carried.
